title: Relative join-prism comparison before the final corner attachment
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices and horns from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. All products, subobjects, unions and pushouts below are degreewise in sets. For simplicial sets $X,Y$, the ordered join has $r$-simplices $X_r\amalg Y_r\amalg\coprod_{a+b+1=r}X_a\times Y_b$, with operators restricting the initial $X$-block and final $Y$-block; empty blocks give the pure-factor summands. Set $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$. Let $A\subseteq B$ be any simplicial subset, let $K$ be any small simplicial set, and let $m\geq0$. Inside $T=(B\star K)\times\Delta^m$ put
$$D=((A\star K)\times\Delta^m)\cup((B\star K)\times\partial\Delta^m).$$
Let $Z$ be the subcomplex generated by $D$ and those simplices $(\sigma,t)$ of $T$ for which every vertex in the $B$-block of $\sigma$ has $t$-coordinate strictly less than $m$. Put
$$R=(A\times\Delta^m)\cup(B\times\partial\Delta^m).$$
There is a canonical injective map $\phi:(B\times\Delta^m)\star K\to T$: on a leading-block simplex retain its $\Delta^m$ coordinates, on the $K$-block use the constant coordinate $m$, and concatenate. The inclusion $D\hookrightarrow Z$ belongs to the weakly saturated closure of the inner horn inclusions $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, $0<i<n$, where weak saturation includes isomorphisms, pushouts, small transfinite compositions and retracts. The restrictions of $\phi$ and the inclusions give a pushout, equivalently the canonical map $$Z\amalg_{R\star K}((B\times\Delta^m)\star K)\longrightarrow T$$ is an isomorphism.
No finiteness, nonemptiness or quasicategory hypothesis is imposed on $A,B,K$.

source.place: Agent formulation of the relative filtration in proof of Proposition B.1.9, cases (B1 prime) and (C2 prime), printed pp.1478-1480; the inner stages use HTT Lemma 2.1.2.3 and Corollary 2.1.2.7. Read online 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this simplicial comparison.

proof.text:
For $0\leq i\leq m$, let $E_i$ be $D$ together with all simplices whose $B$-block coordinates are $<i$. This is already a simplicial subset: restriction cannot introduce a new $B$-coordinate and repetition preserves the inequality; pure $K$-simplices satisfy it vacuously and already belong to $(A\star K)\times\Delta^m\subseteq D$. Thus $E_0=D$ and $E_m=Z$. When $m=0$, these are the same set and the first assertion is an identity. Below take $i<m$, so $d=m-i\geq1$, and put
$$P_i=B\times\Delta^{\{0,\ldots,i\}},\quad L_i=(A\times\Delta^{\{0,\ldots,i\}})\cup(B\times\partial\Delta^{\{0,\ldots,i\}}),$$
$$Q_i=K\times\Delta^{\{i,\ldots,m\}},\qquad H_i=K\times\Lambda^{\{i,\ldots,m\}}_0.$$
The horn in this formula omits the face opposite the first vertex $i$: a simplex belongs to it precisely when it misses some vertex strictly greater than $i$. All these products and inclusions are degreewise as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: B.1.9, (B1 prime) and (C2 prime), printed pp.1478-1480: threshold filtration; notation adapted to arbitrary A contained in B.

proof.text: Concatenate the two blocks to define $\psi_i:P_i\star Q_i\to T$: retain the coordinates in $\{0,\ldots,i\}$ on the leading block and those in $\{i,\ldots,m\}$ on the final block. The concatenation is monotone, commutes with operators, and is injective, since a join simplex has a unique block split and restrictions recover both coordinates. Its image lies in $E_{i+1}$. Conversely, a simplex in $E_{i+1}\setminus E_i$ has a nonempty $B$-block with largest coordinate exactly $i$; monotonicity makes its $K$-block coordinates at least $i$. It therefore lies in this image. Pure $K$-simplices are already in $D$; the same recovery formula handles pure $B$-simplices. Hence $E_{i+1}=E_i\cup\operatorname{im}\psi_i$.

source.place: B.1.9, same two cases: the join map for each threshold; explicit degreewise coverage.

proof.text: Inside $P_i\star Q_i$, set $C_i=(L_i\star Q_i)\cup(P_i\star H_i)$. We show $\psi_i^{-1}(E_i)=C_i$. Pure $K$-simplices lie in $D$ and in $L_i\star Q_i$; pure $B$-simplices lie in $D$ because $i<m$, and in $P_i\star H_i$. For a mixed simplex, membership of the leading block in $A\times\Delta^i$ gives membership in $D$. If its leading coordinate misses $a<i$, then no final coordinate can supply $a$, so the whole simplex belongs to the boundary part of $D$. If its leading coordinate misses $i$, it is already in $E_i$. These give $L_i\star Q_i\subseteq\psi_i^{-1}(E_i)$. If the final coordinate misses $a>i$, the leading block cannot supply $a$, giving $P_i\star H_i\subseteq\psi_i^{-1}(E_i)$. Conversely, outside $C_i$ the leading block is outside $A$, covers every $0,\ldots,i$, and the final block covers every $i+1,\ldots,m$. Thus the total coordinate is surjective and the largest leading coordinate is $i$, so it lies outside $E_i$. This proves the equality. Consequently $E_i\hookrightarrow E_{i+1}$ is a pushout of $C_i\hookrightarrow P_i\star Q_i$: glue maps on the two degreewise subsets along this intersection; the glued map commutes with operators and is unique because the subsets cover.

source.place: B.1.9, (B1 prime)/(C2 prime): explicit old-stage inverse image; direct gluing proves the pushout for general A, B.

proof.text: To use the existing right-anodyne results in the required orientation, write $X^{\mathrm{op}}$ for the simplicial set with the same sets of simplices as $X$ and with the operator for $\alpha:[r]\to[s]$ given by the old operator for $\bar\alpha(j)=s-\alpha(r-j)$. The identity $\overline{\beta\alpha}=\bar\beta\bar\alpha$ makes this an involution. It preserves degreewise products, inclusions, pushouts and continuous transfinite composites, as well as retract diagrams. Reversing a simplex's vertex labels gives $(\Delta^n)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\Delta^n$ and $(\Lambda_j^n)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\Lambda_{n-j}^n$, using the horn formula of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Reversing the two ordered join blocks gives $(X\star Y)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong Y^{\mathrm{op}}\star X^{\mathrm{op}}$: in each mixed summand interchange its two entries and reverse the vertex labels of the indexing blocks. These formulas commute with restriction. In particular taking opposites preserves the weakly saturated inner-horn class, since $0<j<n$ implies $0<n-j<n$.

source.place: B.1.9, application of HTT 2.1.2.3 and 2.1.2.7; explicit order reversal to reuse the existing right-anodyne nodes.

proof.text: Identify $\Delta^{\{i,\ldots,m\}}$ with $\Delta^d$. By step 4, $(H_i\hookrightarrow Q_i)^{\mathrm{op}}$ is the product of $K^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $\Lambda_d^d\hookrightarrow\Delta^d$. The latter is one of the right-horn generators, since $d\geq1$ and $0<d\leq d$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-right-anodyne-product] to that generator and the degreewise injection $\varnothing\hookrightarrow K^{\mathrm{op}}$, exchanging the two product coordinates. Its pushout-product is exactly $H_i^{\mathrm{op}}\hookrightarrow Q_i^{\mathrm{op}}$, so this inclusion is right anodyne. No fibrancy or nonemptiness of $K$ is needed.

source.place: B.1.9, intermediate stages: K times the initial horn is left anodyne (HTT Corollary 2.1.2.7), here obtained by opposite right products.

proof.text:
Use the first assertion of [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones], with its right-anodyne inclusion $A\hookrightarrow B$ equal to $H_i^{\mathrm{op}}\hookrightarrow Q_i^{\mathrm{op}}$, and its arbitrary monomorphism $K\hookrightarrow L$ equal to $L_i^{\mathrm{op}}\hookrightarrow P_i^{\mathrm{op}}$. It says that
$$(H_i^{\mathrm{op}}\star P_i^{\mathrm{op}})\cup(Q_i^{\mathrm{op}}\star L_i^{\mathrm{op}})\hookrightarrow Q_i^{\mathrm{op}}\star P_i^{\mathrm{op}}$$
is in the weakly saturated inner-horn class. Taking opposites as in step 4 identifies it with $C_i\hookrightarrow P_i\star Q_i$, which is therefore in that class too. Step 3 makes $E_i\hookrightarrow E_{i+1}$ its pushout, so it is inner anodyne. Their finite composite for $i=0,\ldots,m-1$ is $D\hookrightarrow Z$, proving the first assertion. All objects stay small in the original universe.

source.place: B.1.9, intermediate join attachments in (B1 prime)/(C2 prime); HTT Lemma 2.1.2.3 with the second factor left anodyne.

proof.text: The final join map is $\phi:(B\times\Delta^m)\star K\to T$. In degree $r$, retain the leading block's product coordinates and put coordinate $m$ on every final-block vertex. This is monotone and commutes with restrictions, and recovering the unique join split recovers the leading product simplex and the final $K$-simplex, so it is injective. If a simplex of $T$ is outside $Z$, its $B$-block is nonempty and contains a coordinate $m$. Every later $K$-coordinate is then $m$ by monotonicity, so the simplex lies in $\operatorname{im}\phi$. Thus $T=Z\cup\operatorname{im}\phi$. This also proves coverage when $m=0$, since $Z=D=A\star K$ and $\phi$ is then an isomorphism.

source.place: B.1.9, final join attachment (i=m) of the same two cases: canonical map and coverage.

proof.text: Put $R=(A\times\Delta^m)\cup(B\times\partial\Delta^m)$. We have $\phi^{-1}(Z)=R\star K$. For a mixed simplex in the source, its final coordinates are all $m$. If its leading block belongs to $A$, its image lies in $D$. If its leading coordinate misses $a<m$, the whole coordinate misses $a$, again giving $D$. If the leading coordinate misses $m$, all its leading coordinates are $<m$, giving $Z$. Conversely, a leading block outside $R$ is outside $A$ and covers $0,\ldots,m$; its image is outside $D$ and has a leading vertex at $m$, so is outside $Z$. Pure $K$-simplices lie on both sides, and for pure $B$-simplices membership in $Z$ is exactly membership in $R$: having all coordinates $<m$ already puts them in the boundary. This proves the inverse-image equality, including $m=0$. Since $\phi$ is injective, maps on $Z$ and its image agree precisely when their restrictions to $R\star K$ agree. Glue them in each degree; the rules agree on the intersection and commute with every operator, giving the unique map on $T$. This is the required pushout and proves that its canonical map to $T$ is an isomorphism. Empty factors and $A=B$ satisfy these same degreewise tests.

source.place: B.1.9, final join attachment: explicit intersection and universal property for arbitrary A contained in B.

Steps 1-3: the threshold filtration E_i is closed under operators, psi_i is injective, and psi_i^{-1}(E_i) = (L_i*Q_i) ∪ (P_i*H_i), checked on mixed, pure-B and pure-K simplices; this gives the degreewise pushout. Step 4: taking opposite simplicial sets (op) sends horn Λ_j to Λ_{n-j} and swaps the two factors of a join, so it preserves the inner-anodyne class. Step 5: the right-anodyne product lemma applies with Λ^d_d→Δ^d (d ≥ 1) and the empty set → K^op. Step 6: I checked that the cocone lemma takes its right-anodyne map in the left join factor by a small example ({1}→Δ^1 with Δ^0 gives Λ^2_1, which is inner). After op this gives C_i → P_i*Q_i, and composing the finitely many stages gives D→Z. Steps 7-8: phi is injective, Z ∪ im(phi) = T, and phi^{-1}(Z) = R*K, so the pushout holds. Small cases checked: B=Δ^0, K=Δ^0, m=1 (one inner Λ^2_1 filling and the pushout with Δ^2), and K empty, m=0, A=B, all of which check. With B=Δ^0, A=∅ and with B=Δ^n, A=∂Δ^n, D is exactly the source the parent's (B1)/(C2) products use; the item does not restate a clause of the parent. The proof uses no hypothesis the statement lacks. The two lemmas used are in the item's own unit, so no tool_uses are needed. No SGA citation. No new nodes; the duplicate search found no node stating this filtration or pushout, and the Mathlib searches cover all three kinds. No changes made.

lean.statement: theorem relative_join_prism_comparison {B : SSet.{u}} (A : B.Subcomplex) (K : SSet.{u}) (m : ℕ) : innerAnodyneExtensions (Subcomplex.homOfLE (le_sup_left : relativeJoinPrismDomain A K m ≤ relativeJoinPrismStage A K m)) ∧ ∃ φ : orderedJoinFunctor.obj (B ⊗ Δ[m], K) ⟶ orderedJoinFunctor.obj (B, K) ⊗ Δ[m], RelativeJoinPrismCoordinates B K m φ ∧ Mono φ ∧ ∃ ρ : orderedJoinFunctor.obj ((A.unionProd (boundary m)).toSSet, K) ⟶ (relativeJoinPrismStage A K m).toSSet, IsPushout ρ (orderedJoinFunctor.map ((A.unionProd (boundary m)).ι, 𝟙 K)) (relativeJoinPrismStage A K m).ι φ
lean.note: The auxiliaries construct D and the generated Z as actual subcomplexes of the existing ordered join prism. The comparison is existentially stated with exact projection equations that uniquely determine its concatenated coordinates; no arbitrary comparison is assumed or chosen. IsPushout is the stated equivalent of invertibility of the canonical pushout comparison. The two added landed statement dependencies own orderedJoinFunctor and its pure-block inclusions.
